Palace Hotel Yard
Explosion

Home-made Bomb Believed
Cause ; Riot Vans Arrive ;
Pedestrians Searched

A terrific explosion at the rear of
the Palace Hotel just before noon
yesterday, thought to have been
caused by a cigarette tin type bomb,
sent lunch hour crowds on the Bund
scampering for safety as police with
drawn pistols dashed to the scene.
Clouds of blue smoke drifting up
from the yard at the rear of the
hotel lent weight to the theory that
a bomb had been thrown over the
wall by someone wishing to rid him-
self of the dangerous object, prob-
ably on account of the close proxim-
ity of a police search party. Inside
the yard, however, except for a few
marks on the wall, there were no
signs of there having been an ex-
plosion.

The explosion, which occurred at
11.50 a.m., was heard over a wide
area, and a reporter from the "North-
China Daily News" who arrived at
the scene immediately after the
detonation found the lane between
the Chartered Bank building and the
Palace Hotel jammed with a crowd
of curious sightseers. Over the
heads of the crowd a pall of blue
smoke was being blown about by the
breeze, but nowhere was there any
sign of damage.

Inside the yard no splinters or evi-
dence of a bomb having been thrown
could be found, and an official of
the Palace Hotel was at a loss to
explain the cause of the explosion.
The yard does not contain any
articles such as gas containers, re-
frigerators or domestic appliances
which are likely to explode through
the heat and, therefore, the theory
is held that a home-made bomb
was thrown by a person or persons
unknown in an effort to get rid of it
quickly.

Riot Vans Arrive

An ambulance and police in bullet-
proof jackets were quickly on the
scene, followed by two riot vans.
Working in separate parties the
police, with drawn pistols, scoured
the street, stopping all persons to
search them for arms or other articles
carried by the terrorists. Except for
slight cuts on the back of the neck
sustained by a Chinese in the yard
at the time, no one was injured by
the explosion and the services of the
ambulance were not required.

The large lunch-hour crowds which
visit the Palace Hotel each day had
not arrived when the explosion oc-
curred, but the few people who were
sitting in the grill room, which ad-
joins the yard, were deafened by the
noise of the explosion. Their fears,
however, were quickly allayed when
it became known that there was no
danger and that nobody had been
seriously injured.

An official of the hotel stated that
after the explosion the yard was
filled with a smell resembling that
of acetylene, which, at first, made
him think there had been an explo-
sion in the kitchens. A glance
around, however, showed no signs
of this.

During the afternoon three Japan-
ese constables of the S.M.P. and sen-
tries from the Seaforth Highlanders
were posted in the lane, and a sentry
also stood at the Nanking Road en-
trance to the kitchens.

（批：Lilo 8k 18）

汇中饭店庭院
爆炸事件

疑为自制炸弹所致；防暴车抵达；
行人受搜身检查

昨日临近中午时分，汇中饭店（Palace Hotel）后方发生剧烈爆炸，据信系由一种香烟罐式炸弹引起，致使外滩午餐时段的人群惊慌逃窜以寻求安全，警察拔出手枪冲向现场。从饭店后院的庭院中飘起阵阵蓝烟，这进一步佐证了这样一种推测：有人因靠近警方搜查队，急于摆脱这一危险物品，遂将炸弹扔过墙头。然而，在庭院内部，除墙上留有几处痕迹外，并无任何爆炸迹象。

此次爆炸发生于上午11时50分，声响传遍广大区域。《字林西报》（North-China Daily News）的一名记者在爆炸发生后立即抵达现场，发现麦加利银行（Chartered Bank）大楼与汇中饭店之间的弄堂挤满了好奇的围观者。人群头顶上方，一团团蓝烟随风飘散，但四处均未见受损迹象。

在庭院内，未发现任何碎片或炸弹被投掷的证据，汇中饭店的一名官员也无法解释爆炸原因。该庭院内并未存放煤气罐、冰箱或家用电器等可能因受热而爆炸的物品，因此，目前的推测是，一名或多名身份不明者为迅速处理掉一枚自制炸弹而将其投掷于此。

防暴车抵达

一辆救护车和身穿防弹背心的警察迅速赶至现场，随后两辆防暴车也相继到达。警察分成若干小组，拔出手枪，对街道进行彻底搜查，拦下所有行人，搜查其是否携带武器或恐怖分子常用的其他物品。除一名当时在庭院内的华人颈部后方受轻微割伤外，爆炸未造成任何人受伤，故无需动用救护车服务。

爆炸发生时，每日光顾汇中饭店的大量午餐人群尚未抵达，但少数坐在毗邻庭院的烧烤餐厅（grill room）内的客人被爆炸声震得耳聋目眩。然而，当得知并无危险且无人受重伤后，他们的恐惧很快得以平息。

饭店一名官员表示，爆炸后庭院内弥漫着一股类似乙炔的气味，这起初让他以为是厨房发生了爆炸。然而，环顾四周，并未发现此类迹象。

下午期间，三名上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）的日本巡捕以及海福尔高地团（Seaforth Highlanders）的哨兵被部署在该弄堂内，另有一名哨兵驻守在通往厨房的南京路入口处。

（批注：Lilo 8k 18）

Palace Hotel and vicinity
Detective Office.

Explosion which occurred inside a narrow
lane adjoining The Palace Hotel premises,
No. 19 The Bund 30-7-38.

At 12noon 30-7-38, S/Inspt. Liao Wei Woo attached
to Central Station, reported by telephone to the effect
that an explosion had just occurred at the Palace Hotel,
No. 19 The Bund which was believed to be the result of
a bomb having been thrown at the premises.

The station alarm was immediately rung, which
resulted in all available personnel of this station
attending and proceeding to the scene, C/I Barry in charge.
Enquiries made by D.Inspt. Telfer, D.S. Guess, D.S.I.
Yang Pei Shang, C.D.S.203, C.D.C. 148 and the undersigned,
ascertained the followings:-

At 11.55a.m. 30-7-38, a loud explosion was heard to
take place inside a narrow lane which extends along the
South side of the Palace Hotel, whilst persons in the
vicinity and employees of the hotel attracted by the
noise attended the scene, saw large clouds of a bluish-
grey coloured smoke filling the lane.

An employee of the hotel named Shien Shien Foo
(徐金福) 19, Cook, who was at that time obtaining some
fresh air after a period of employment in the kitchen,
was proceeding West along the lane when in his rear he
heard the explosion and was suddenly struck in the neck
near to the base of his head, this employee immediatel-

中午12时至下午3时
1938年7月30日。

汇中饭店及周边地区
侦探办公室。

1938年7月30日，发生在毗邻汇中饭店产业（外滩19号）的一条狭窄弄堂内的爆炸事件。

1938年7月30日中午12时，隶属中央巡捕房的副督察廖伟武（Liao Wei Woo，音译）通过电话报告称，外滩19号汇中饭店刚刚发生爆炸，据信系有人向该处投掷炸弹所致。

站内警报随即拉响，本站所有可用人员随即集结并赶赴现场，由警长巴里（Barry）负责指挥。经副侦探督察特尔弗（Telfer）、侦探警佐格斯（Guess）、侦探副督察杨佩尚（Yang Pei Shang，音译）、中国侦探警佐203号、中国侦探警长148号及本报告人调查，查明以下情况：

1938年7月30日上午11时55分，有人听到一声巨响，爆炸发生在沿汇中饭店南侧延伸的一条狭窄弄堂内。附近的居民及饭店员工被噪音吸引赶到现场，看到大量蓝灰色烟雾弥漫在弄堂中。

饭店一名雇员徐金福（Shien Shien Foo），19岁，厨师，当时刚在厨房工作了一段时间，正出来呼吸新鲜空气。他正沿着弄堂向西行走时，听到身后传来爆炸声，颈部靠近后脑勺基部突然受到撞击，该雇员立即

away from the scene of the explosion not being aware of
what had taken place. The injury is very slight and was
deemed by the injured person not to require treatment at
a hospital.
Shortly afterwards when the smoke had cleared away
F.S. Lawman attended the scene and found that apparently
a bomb of some type had been thrown over a wall which is
about 8 feet in height and extends towards the West along
the South boundary of the Palace Hotel premises, dividing
the hotel narrow lane which has an average width of about
5 feet from the lane which extends West on the North side
of the Chartered Bank of India, Australia and China, No.
18 The Bund.
The bomb having apparently struck the South wall of
the hotel about 4 feet from the ground and near to an iron
barred window of the hotel provision and store rooms and
about 30 feet West from the Bund.
F.S. Lawman after his arrival saw a large sized tin
in the centre of which was embedded amidst a powdered
substance such as cement, a cigarette tin which was also
believed to be a bomb, this tin being found inside a box
containing sand near to the place of the explosion, the
article was immediately placed into a pail containing
water to render it harmless.

离开爆炸现场，并不知晓发生了何事。伤势非常轻微，伤者认为无需去医院治疗。
不久后，待烟雾散去，法医劳曼（Lawman）抵达现场，发现显然有一枚某种类型的炸弹被扔过了一堵墙。该墙高约8英尺，沿汇中饭店产业南界向西延伸，将平均宽度约5英尺的饭店狭窄弄堂与位于印度新金山中国汇理银行（Chartered Bank of India, Australia and China，外滩18号）北侧向西延伸的弄堂隔开。
炸弹显然击中了饭店南墙，位置距地面约4英尺，靠近饭店食品和储藏室的一扇装有铁栅栏的窗户，且位于距外滩以西约30英尺处。
劳曼法医到达后，看到一个大型铁皮箱，其中心嵌有水泥状粉末物质，其中还有一个香烟罐，也被认为是炸弹。该铁皮箱是在爆炸地点附近的一个盛沙箱子内发现的。该物品随即被放入一桶水中以使其失效。

of the bank overlooking this lane, but failed to locate any
who
person/admitted having witnessed any suspicious
circumstances likely to be connected with this explosion.

The force of the explosion had caused numerous small
pieces of the building wall and the lane wall surfaces to
be chipped, a number of metal fragments believed to have
been the contents of the bomb were found inside the lane,
also a quantity of slightly yellow coloured pieces of
glass, some discoloured and torn pieces of a Chinese
newspaper and one small length of red coloured string
being found near to the scene of the explosion.

The manager of the hotel Mr. G. Herzel, the
compradore Sang Moh Cheu (张茂秋) and other hotel
employees in positions of authority were questioned to
ascertain if possible a motive for this bomb having been
thrown at the premises, to which the only reason that
could be offered was that the compradore was believed to
have purchased quantities of Japanese products, but
eventually when the compradore was located and interrogated it was found that the only Japanese purchases effected
are made by a Mr. Hugo per telephone and that same are
delivered to the hotel, this therefore would not appear to
be the reason for this incident.

There has been no recent disturbances amongst the
hotel staff likely to be attributed to the cause of this
page_data.zh:
杂项案卷 775/38号 (C)。

第1张/共3张。

未能找到任何承认目睹过可能与此次爆炸有关的可疑情况的人。

爆炸的威力导致建筑墙体和弄堂墙面的许多小块碎片剥落。在弄堂内发现了若干金属碎片，据信为炸弹内含物；此外，还发现了少量略带黄色的玻璃碎片、一些变色且撕裂的中文报纸碎片，以及在爆炸现场附近发现的一小段红色细绳。

饭店经理赫泽尔先生（Mr. G. Herzel）、买办张茂秋（Sang Moh Cheu）及其他具有管理职位的饭店员工接受了问询，以期查明有人向该处投掷炸弹的动机。对此，唯一提出的理由是，据信该买办购买了大量日本产品。但最终找到并审问该买办后发现，唯一的日本商品采购是由一位雨果先生（Mr. Hugo，音译）通过电话进行的，并直接送至饭店。因此，这似乎并非此次事件的原因。

饭店员工近期并未发生任何可能导致此次

page_data.en:
Misc. 775/38(C).
1/sheet 4.

incident, although there are a number of Japanese persons
residing inside the hotel, their rooms are so situated as
to be not near to the scene of the explosion, and they
are considered not to be of such important rank that would
justify any action as the above being taken against them
by any persons.

Mr. C. Fletcher of the S.M.C./P.H. Dept. was
communicated with and attended this station and examined
the object obtained which had been removed to this Station
and was believed to be a bomb, it being subsequently found
that the cigarette tin also contained powdered cement and
that same had apparently been left behind by employees of
a building contractor who had renovated the hotel premises.

The fragments obtained were also examined by Mr.
Fletcher and one jagged piece of metal and one piece of
glass removed for examination, it being believed that
same were part of the bomb thrown, which is considered
to be of the cigarette tin (Canister) type of bomb.

The scene of the explosion was again visited and
a thorough search made to find if possible, parts of the
cigarette tin used in the construction of the bomb, but
same could not be found.

In view of the above and lack of a motive for the
bombing being ascertained it is considered most probably
that the persons firstly in possession of the bomb whilst
page_data.zh:
杂项案卷 775/38号(C)。
第1张/共4张。

事件的骚乱。尽管有数名日本人居住在饭店内，但其房间位置并不靠近爆炸现场，且他们的地位被认为并不重要，不足以成为任何人采取上述行动的理由。

已联系工部局公共卫生处（S.M.C./P.H. Dept.）的弗莱彻先生（Mr. C. Fletcher），他来到本站并检查了被移至本站、据信为炸弹的物品。随后发现，该香烟罐内也装有水泥粉，这显然是翻修饭店产业的建筑承包商雇员遗留下来的。

弗莱彻先生也对获得的碎片进行了检查，并取走了一块锯齿状金属片和一块玻璃片以供检验。据信这些碎片是被投掷炸弹的一部分，该炸弹被认为是香烟罐（筒状）式炸弹。

再次勘察了爆炸现场，并进行了彻底搜索，以期找到用于制造炸弹的香烟罐部件，但未能找到。

鉴于上述情况及未能查明爆炸动机，极有可能的情况是，最初持有炸弹的人在

page_data.en:
Misc. 775/38(C).
1/sheet 5.

proceeding along the Lane observed some activity possibly
on the part of a member of the I.R.A., such as searching
some person and being apprehensive, he got rid of the
bomb by entering the alleyway and throwing it over the
wall, this action in itself would be so simple that it
could easily be performed and pass unnoticed, the person
concerned then made his getaway leisurely without any
interference and apparently unobserved.

Mr. H.D.M. Robertson D.O. "A" Division, Mr. Alers
D.D.O. "A" Division attended the scene, whilst Mr.
Bourne Commissioner of Police and Captain Smythe O.B.E.
D.C. Divisions were informed of the above by telephone.

沿弄堂行进时，观察到某些活动，可能是爱尔兰共和军（I.R.A.）成员的行动，例如搜查某人。出于担忧，他进入小巷并将炸弹扔过墙头，以此摆脱炸弹。这一举动本身非常简单，可以轻易完成且不引人注意。随后，相关人员从容逃离，未受任何干扰，且显然未被察觉。

“A”分区侦探督察长罗伯逊先生（Mr. H.D.M. Robertson）、“A”分区副侦探督察长阿勒斯先生（Mr. Alers）抵达现场。同时，警务处处长伯恩先生（Mr. Bourne）及分区副处长史密斯上尉（Captain Smythe, O.B.E.）已通过电话获知上述情况。
